# Fires Fires come in two forms, gas and tile based. Gas fires are incredibly dangerous and fast spreading, most commonly due to plasma gas igniting. Tile fires can be started from a variety of sources and can take over large sections of rooms if left unattended, while producing smoke.
Firelocks and doors can help hold off fires of both types, holding back both the flames and smoke. Opening one even for a moment can let it spread outwards, so be prepared to fight it if you do.
## Combating Fires All fires need oxygen to burn, and removing it can easily extinguish a fire, if you can handle the aftermath.
More often then not though, the fires you will be handling will be tile fires however, and spacing might be overkill for them. If they're available, a [color=#f39f27]Firefighter[/color] is best equipped to handle a blaze, but there's still plenty around you can use.
Fire Closets and Extinguisher Cabinets can be found around the station in the walls and in maintenance, and have everything you could need for basic fire fighting.
Firesuits and helmets can protect you from the flames, while a gas mask can help keep smoke out of your lungs. Fire extinguishers can have the safety removed by hitting [color=yellow][bold][keybind="ActivateItemInHand"][/bold][/color] and then can be sprayed as expected. You can refill them with most water sources by simply interacting with them.
## Tips - Try to manage or avoid inhaling smoke by using internals or a gas mask, inhaling too much can give a cough among other temporary heal ailments. If you find yourself with any of these just breath some clean air and you'll recover shortly. - Tile fires can only spread so much, and eventually will burn out. If a situation seems hopeless it can be left at the price of smoke buildup and loss of access to the burning room. - Bring a water tank to handle larger fires, sometimes basic fire extinguishers can't handle a blaze.
